scenes.title: narrated
scenes.subtitle: Narrated videos from a JSON script. Built for AI agents.
scenes.say: This video was written as a JSON file, and rendered by narrated. No editor, no browser, no API key.

scenes.title: The problem
items: Every agent makes videos a different way
Narration has to be asked for
scenes.say: Agents are asked for videos all the time. But every agent builds them a different way. The voice changes every time. Narration has to be requested explicitly. And a render can take ten minutes.

scenes.title: The fix: one standard pipeline
items: Write scenes, each with a line to say
narrated voices it with one consistent voice
Scenes are timed to the real audio
Captions, MP4, SRT and a report come out
scenes.say: narrated makes it one standard pipeline. You write scenes, and each scene has a line to say. narrated voices it locally, with the same voice every time. Every scene is timed to the real audio length. And out comes an MP4, captions, and a JSON report.

scenes.title: The whole API
scenes.say: The whole API is one function. Pass a list of scenes. Every scene says something.

scenes.title: Gameplay clips
scenes.subtitle: Drop in any mp4 — it loops, crops and gets captioned
scenes.say: Gameplay footage and screen recordings drop right in. They are cropped to fit, looped if they are short, and captioned automatically.

scenes.title: Screenshots
scenes.subtitle: Slow push-in, lower third, captions
scenes.say: Screenshots get a slow push in, so stills never feel dead.

scenes.title: Before vs after
scenes.say: Before, every video was a one off. With narrated, it is one spec format, one voice, narration by default, and a parallel, cached render.

scenes.label: API keys, cloud services or browsers required
scenes.say: And it needs zero API keys, zero cloud services, and zero browsers.

scenes.text: When an agent needs a video, it should reach for one tool.
scenes.say: When an agent needs a video, it should reach for one tool.

scenes.title: Try it
scenes.say: To try it, install it from GitHub. Run init to get a starter script. Then render it.
